newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates seen easing off highs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates seen easing off highs.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose further on Tuesday as liquidity was still unevenly divided in the market. But dealers said the market should come off its peak as some participants had nearly made up for their shortage.
Call money was bid at a high of 3.31 percent today, but most business was done at a slightly lower level, dealers said. Call was bid between 3.18 and 3.31 versus 3.12 percent bid on Monday.
Deposits from one month up to one year were trading at an unchanged level. Three-month deposits were glued to yesterday's 3.12 percent bid.
The guilder was stronger against the German mark, trading at 112.4775 per 100 marks versus 112.4925 on Monday.
